task.name: A catalog entry names an upstream identifier the provider has retired, so a superseded model is selected and priced from a rate card that no longer applies
task.story_text:
## Observed

A model identifier that a provider has retired continues to be offered for routing, and the spend it
records is computed from a rate card the provider has replaced.

Model identity is declared in three places that are maintained by hand and never checked against the
provider: a shipped catalog entry, a canonical-alias map, and an accounting table. All three still
carry an identifier the provider announced for retirement and has since removed from its published
model list. The identifier has not stopped resolving upstream — calls made through it complete with
exit 0 and return token counts — so nothing in the system observes that the name now designates a
different model than the one whose capability, tier and price were recorded against it. The
accounting table's own comments still describe the entry as an alias for a model generation two
releases old.

The consequences are not confined to a stale label:

Spend is misreported in the direction that matters. Two runs on 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-09 each
recorded roughly `$3.7` of estimated cost against ~6.4M input and ~78k output tokens. Priced against
the rate card the provider currently publishes for the model the identifier now resolves to, the same
usage is several times cheaper. The estimate is not marked provisional; it is `cost_provenance:
estimated` like every other estimate, and it feeds budget ceilings, cost-target routing and price
tie-breaks.

The routing declaration no longer describes the model being invoked. The entry is banded as a strong
reasoning model, and it was returned to the reviewer pool on that basis. Every recorded run shows
zero reasoning tokens, and the adapter for this provider passes no request-level control for
reasoning behaviour at all — it forwards a model name and a response format and nothing else. Where
a provider has moved reasoning from a model-name distinction to a request parameter, an identifier
inherited from the old scheme cannot express the mode it was banded for.

The cost model has no place for a rate the provider bills separately. Every recorded run shows zero
cached input tokens, and there is no cached-input rate in the catalog schema for this provider, so a
tier the provider prices roughly two orders of magnitude below its uncached rate is neither requested
nor accounted for.

## Expected

An identifier the system offers for routing is one the provider currently serves, and it designates
the same model whose capability, tier and price were recorded against it. Where a provider retires,
re-points or re-scopes an identifier, that is discoverable from the system's own configuration rather
than from a run whose output happens to look wrong — and discoverable at the point configuration is
loaded, when an operator can still act on it, not after a run has spent against it.

An identifier that silently continues to resolve after it has been retired is the more dangerous case
than one that stops working, because a hard failure is self-announcing and a soft substitution is
not. Where the system cannot establish that a name still means what was recorded about it, that
uncertainty is stated rather than absorbed, and a declaration that cannot be confirmed does not carry
the same weight in selection as one that can.

Recorded cost reflects what the provider actually bills for the invocation that was made. Where a
provider prices a class of input at a distinct rate, the system can express that rate and account for
it, rather than pricing every input at the highest of the provider's rates. A cost figure that is
known to be derived from a rate card that may no longer apply is distinguishable from one that is
not, so a downstream decision made on price can tell how much the price is worth.

Where a provider expresses a behavioural mode as a request parameter rather than as a distinct model
name, the system can express that mode. A role assigned a model for a property that property must be
requested to obtain is invoked in a way that actually requests it.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom.** A model routed as a strong reasoning reviewer records zero reasoning tokens,
zero cached input, and an estimated cost several times the provider's published rate — while
completing successfully, so nothing flags it.

**Evidence.**

- `src/theforge/config/data/models.yaml:283-310` — two shipped catalog entries pin identifiers the
  provider has retired, with input/output rates from the superseded rate card and a
  `pricing_provenance` naming the retired identifier as its own source.
- `src/theforge/config/models.py:216-217` — the canonical-alias map resolves the same retired
  identifiers, so a project-level reference to them resolves cleanly rather than failing.
- `src/theforge/runners/schema_utils.py:87-90` — the accounting table carries four entries for this
  provider, two of them commented as aliases of a model generation two releases old, at the same
  superseded rates.
- `forge.yaml:101` — the entry is in `models.enabled`, unbenched 2026-08-08 under #2207, which
  returned it to the reviewer pool.
- `.forge/audits/runs/5fd68935e09b.json` — two review agents, `success: true`, `exit_code: 0`,
  `cost_provenance: estimated`, `$3.727` and `$3.683`; `usage.thinking_tokens: 0` and
  `usage.cache_read_tokens: 0` on both.
- `src/theforge/runners/adapters/deepseek.py:32-47` — the adapter forwards a model name and a
  response format; it passes no reasoning-mode parameter and reads no reasoning-token field.
- Provider's published change log and model list, retrieved 2026-08-09: the identifiers in use are
  absent, superseded by two current identifiers with a different rate card and a separately-billed
  cached-input rate; reasoning is now a request-level toggle rather than a model-name distinction.

**Ruled out.** Not an auth or availability failure: calls complete with exit 0 and real token counts.
Not the missing-accounting-table case of #2335: this identifier is present in the table, so no
cost-unknown warning fires and the wrong price is recorded confidently. Not a per-run anomaly: every
recorded run for this identifier shows the same zero reasoning tokens and zero cached input. Not the
config duplicate-declaration check, which compares project configuration against the shipped catalog
and has no notion of what the provider currently serves.

**Confirmed cause.** Model identity and price are hand-maintained in three code-side locations with
no mechanism that compares them against the provider, and no mechanism that distinguishes an
identifier still served from one that resolves only because the provider is being lenient. A retired
identifier therefore stays selectable indefinitely, carrying declarations that describe a model it no
longer designates, and the failure surfaces only as quiet inaccuracy in cost and capability rather
than as an error.

- **Affected code path:** `theforge.config.data.models` catalog entries, `theforge.config.models`
  canonical-alias map, `theforge.runners.schema_utils.PRICING_TABLE`, and
  `theforge.runners.adapters.deepseek._run_deepseek`.

**Fix-success criterion.** The identifiers offered for this provider are ones it currently serves,
priced from the rate card in force including its separately-billed input tier, with the behavioural
mode the routing declaration claims actually requested at invocation; and a subsequent retirement of
any provider identifier is surfaced from configuration rather than inferred from a run's output.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5 threads reasoning into a code path review runs never take. It says to pass the reasoning option into _run_deepseek and to include the request-level reasoning parameter when invoking _run_openai_chat, while keeping the behavior isolated to the DeepSeek adapter. The runs in the diagnosis are review agents, which dispatch through _LOOP_RUNNERS to _run_loop_deepseek (src/theforge/runners/api.py:848). That function never calls _run_deepseek or _run_openai_chat; it calls _make_openai_chat_adapter(profile, secrets, client=client) at api.py:863, which lives in src/theforge/runners/adapters/openai.py:229 and is shared with _run_loop_openai (api.py:744). Reviews also route through _make_deepseek_finalizer. Implemented exactly as written, review invocations still send no reasoning parameter and the fix-success criterion (the behavioural mode actually requested at invocation) is unmet.
  Suggestion: Bring src/theforge/runners/adapters/openai.py into Step 5's file list and add a provider-scoped extra-request-kwargs seam through _make_openai_chat_adapter and the finalizer, or give DeepSeek its own chat adapter. Drop the 'isolated to the DeepSeek adapter' constraint - it is not achievable for the loop path as the code is currently structured.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Cached-input accounting is blocked upstream of pricing, and the blocking file is unscoped. Step 4 confines cached-input work to schema_utils.py and models.yaml, but estimate_cost already accepts cached_input_tokens, already subtracts them from uncached input, and already prices them at cached_input_rate_mult (src/theforge/runners/schema_utils.py:207-247) - the subtraction logic the step proposes to add exists. The actual gap is that the OpenAI-compatible adapter DeepSeek reuses hardcodes cache_read_tokens=0 at src/theforge/runners/adapters/openai.py:67, :191 and :368, so usage.cache_read_tokens is structurally always 0 for this provider regardless of any rate change - exactly what the audit shows. DeepSeek reports cache hits in a provider-specific usage field, not the OpenAI field. adapters/openai.py appears in no step, so as scoped the cached-rate behaviour cannot be demonstrated by anything but a synthetic unit test.
  Suggestion: Add src/theforge/runners/adapters/openai.py to Step 4 and do two things: read DeepSeek's provider-specific cache-hit usage field into ModelUsage instead of hardcoding 0, and make the cached rate provider-specific rather than the single shared CACHED_INPUT_RATE_MULT - DeepSeek's cached tier is roughly two orders of magnitude below uncached, not the shared default.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's forge.yaml action rests on a false premise and targets an undeliverable file. It says to replace enabled DeepSeek model keys in forge.yaml with the new current catalog keys, but there are no enabled DeepSeek keys: forge.yaml:101 is commented out ('# - deepseek/deepseek-reasoner/api') and the comment records RE-BENCHED 2026-08-09 (run 040bc2e87ab4) for a recurring non-delivery failure, one day after the #2207 unbench. The spec's claim that the entry is in models.enabled and unbenched 2026-08-08 is stale. Following Step 2 literally would add the new identifiers as enabled, silently reversing a bench decision made two days ago - a behaviour change outside this story. Separately, 'git ls-files -v forge.yaml' reports S (skip-worktree) in this worktree, so any edit the dev makes to it cannot be staged or delivered.
  Suggestion: Drop forge.yaml from the plan's file list entirely. Re-enabling DeepSeek is an operator decision outside this story, and renaming an identifier inside a comment is not worth the delivery hazard of editing a skip-worktree file.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] PRICING_TABLE's value shape has a caller outside Step 4's file list. PRICING_TABLE is dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float]] and is unpacked positionally at src/theforge/runners/runner_claude.py:198 ('in_rate, out_rate = PRICING_TABLE[('anthropic', key)]') and membership-checked at src/theforge/assignment.py:2220. Neither file is in Step 4's list, so widening the value tuple to carry a cached rate would break runner_claude.py at runtime.
  Suggestion: Keep the two-tuple value shape and carry any per-provider cached rate in a sidecar map keyed the same way, or update runner_claude.py:198 and assignment.py:2220 in the same step. Citing the caller here so it is not discovered after the fact.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 leaves the provider manifest artifact unspecified as to where it lives and what happens on a miss. Validating against a checked-in provider model manifest rather than a live provider call is the right call, but the plan does not name the artifact's location or say whether a missing manifest entry raises or merely marks the declaration unverified. The preflight flagged exactly this choice as materially changing blast radius: a hard failure would break config load for every user the next time an unrelated provider entry is added.
  Suggestion: Name the manifest file location alongside src/theforge/config/data/models.yaml, and state that a missing manifest entry marks the entry unverified (dropping its selection weight) rather than raising at load.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] To avoid circular dependencies during module loading, any import of the model registry or catalog parser inside schema_utils.py (e.g. for deriving PRICING_TABLE entries dynamically) must be deferred/local to the lookup function, since config.models already performs an import-time load of schema_utils.py.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The checked-in provider model manifest config file should be placed as a JSON or YAML artifact inside src/theforge/config/data/ next to models.yaml, keeping config files well-localized.

findings.description: The fix-success criterion bundles three functionally independent changes under one root-cause diagnosis: (1) a config-load-time mechanism to detect when a provider has retired/re-pointed a model identifier, (2) pricing-model changes to add a separately-billed cached-input rate tier and mark cost estimates as unconfirmed when identity can't be verified, and (3) a behavioral change to the deepseek adapter to pass a request-level reasoning-mode parameter. These touch different subsystems (config/catalog validation, the accounting/pricing schema, and a provider adapter's request construction) and would produce unrelated diffs reviewable independently. Bundling them means a single PR mixes a validation feature, a schema/pricing feature, and an adapter behavior fix.

stories.name: Detect retired/re-pointed provider model identifiers at config load
acs: Loading configuration for a provider whose currently-published model list no longer includes a catalog/alias-map/accounting-table identifier surfaces a discoverable warning at load time, not after a run has spent against it.
A model identifier whose provider-side identity cannot be confirmed is flagged as unconfirmed rather than treated identically to a verified declaration in routing selection.

stories.name: Support separately-billed cached-input pricing and mark unverifiable cost estimates
acs: The pricing schema can express a distinct rate for cached input tokens for providers that bill it separately, and recorded cost uses that rate when cached tokens are present.
A cost estimate derived from a rate card tied to an identifier whose provider-side identity is unconfirmed is distinguishable (e.g. via provenance) from an estimate tied to a confirmed identifier.

stories.name: Request reasoning mode via request parameter for providers that expose it that way
acs: For a provider that exposes reasoning as a request-level toggle rather than a distinct model name, a role routed to a reasoning-banded model on that provider issues a request that actually requests reasoning behavior.
Runs made in reasoning mode against such a provider record non-zero reasoning tokens when the provider returns them.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Replace the retired DeepSeek model declarations with current, versioned provider identities, then make catalog loading and accounting carry enough metadata to detect stale provider IDs, price cached input separately, and request declared reasoning behavior at invocation.

steps.description: Extend the packaged model catalog schema to represent provider verification, cached-input pricing, and request-level behavior.
steps.details: Add optional fields to the existing model identity/catalog parse path for provider-served identity status, provider verification provenance or checked timestamp, cached input cost rate, and provider request options such as reasoning mode. Update DeepSeek entries to current provider-served identifiers and rates, including cached-input rate and a reasoning-mode declaration for the strong reasoning entry.

steps.description: Remove legacy aliases that keep retired DeepSeek identifiers resolving as selectable models.
steps.details: Update _LEGACY_MODEL_KEY_ALIASES so retired DeepSeek identifiers no longer silently normalize to active catalog entries. Replace enabled DeepSeek model keys in forge.yaml with the new current catalog keys, or leave the retired names only as explicit rejected/diagnostic aliases if existing validation supports that pattern.

steps.description: Surface provider identity drift during configuration/catalog load.
steps.details: Validate packaged catalog entries against a checked-in provider model manifest or equivalent low-dependency config artifact, not a live provider call. Fail or clearly mark entries whose provider identifier is retired, unverified, or missing from the manifest so they do not carry normal selection weight.

steps.description: Unify runner pricing with the catalog metadata and account for cached input tokens.
steps.details: Replace or derive the DeepSeek PRICING_TABLE entries from the updated catalog rates so retired identifiers and superseded comments disappear. Add cached-input pricing support to the cost calculation path using usage.cache_read_tokens when present, subtracting cached tokens from normal input billing as appropriate, and make provenance distinguish stale or unverified rate data from ordinary estimates.

steps.description: Thread declared DeepSeek reasoning behavior into the provider adapter.
steps.details: Pass the catalog/profile request option for reasoning mode through the existing runner-facing profile/config object into _run_deepseek, and include the provider's request-level reasoning parameter when invoking _run_openai_chat. Keep the behavior isolated to the DeepSeek adapter.

steps.description: Add focused regression coverage for catalog validation, alias rejection, pricing, and DeepSeek request options.
steps.details: Add tests proving retired DeepSeek identifiers are not selectable through catalog load or normalize_model_key, current identifiers validate, cached-input tokens use the cached rate, stale/unverified pricing provenance is distinguishable, and the DeepSeek adapter includes the reasoning request option without invoking real provider CLIs.

criteria_mapping.criterion: An identifier the system offers for routing is one the provider currently serves, and it designates the same model whose capability, tier and price were recorded against it.
A subsequent retirement of any provider identifier is surfaced from configuration rather than inferred from a run's output.
Recorded cost reflects what the provider actually bills for the invocation that was made, including a separately priced cached-input tier.
A cost figure derived from a rate card that may no longer apply is distinguishable from one that is not.
Where a provider expresses a behavioural mode as a request parameter rather than as a distinct model name, the system can express that mode and invokes it.

risks.description: The spec does not name the provider's current DeepSeek identifiers, exact request parameter, or exact rate values.
risks.mitigation: Have the dev agent verify against the provider model list and changelog dated at implementation time, then encode that snapshot in the checked-in manifest/provenance instead of relying on live network checks.

risks.description: Deriving runner pricing from catalog data may expose existing duplication assumptions around PRICING_TABLE.
risks.mitigation: Keep the first implementation narrow to DeepSeek and preserve existing table behavior for other providers unless the local code makes a shared helper clearly smaller.

risks.description: Changing legacy alias behavior may break project configs that still reference retired names.
risks.mitigation: Prefer a precise validation error with the replacement key over permissive remapping, because configuration load is the integrity boundary.
